primary_sources.title: MetaQuotes copy_rates_range Python reference
primary_sources.support: The API reference describes returned tick/bar timestamps as UTC and requires UTC query datetimes. This is direct API documentation, not an observation proving that this stored historical file follows it.

primary_sources.title: FP Markets server-time FAQ
primary_sources.support: The current platform server uses GMT+2/GMT+3 to align daily candles with New York close. Platform display convention alone does not identify API field encoding.

primary_sources.title: FP Markets MetaTrader PDS, 29 March 2021, section 5.4, printed page 47
primary_sources.support: The margin-FX/metals financing section equates New York local 17:00 with server 00:00. This historical statement supports the server convention, not an individual cash-index historical API timestamp.

primary_sources.title: FP Markets trading hours
primary_sources.support: The current table places US30/US500/US100 at 01:00-24:00 in its displayed GMT+2/GMT+3 convention. This resembles most observed raw daily boundaries but is not a dated 2024/2025 field certificate.

bounded_dated_search.scope: Six primary-domain search queries across 2024/March and 2025/March/November server-DST terms plus the index-hours table. Promotion pages and locale mirrors are not historical trading-clock authority.
bounded_dated_search.finding: No source-specific dated 2024/2025 transition notice or original field-serialization certificate was located in this bounded search. This does not assert that none exists elsewhere.

original_provenance.scope_limit: Receipt names an old contract and runtime but no producer script or raw-field offset witness; no old runtime or broker API was executed.

unresolved_both_symbols: 2025-03-11..13 start 00:00 and have an internal missing 01:00..01:59 hour
2025-03-14 starts 00:00, has the same missing hour, and ends 23:34

inference_limits: The majority daily pattern is circumstantial support for server-style labels, not proof of absolute UTC. API UTC documentation and the platform convention cannot be collapsed into one assumption.
The March 2025 exceptions are shared by both studied cash-index series; they cannot be dismissed as the already known ETF-only issue. Their cause is unresolved without independent source evidence.
Neither greater event coverage under the nominal bridge nor a hypothetical market reaction can choose an offset. No timestamps or dates were shifted/deleted.
Public documentation may contain unrelated illustrative historical prices; none is a candidate input or price/return calculation. No 2026 candidate price/outcome opens.
next_source_requirement: Before any exact external-session correction, obtain an independently attributable mapping from the original time field to the relevant historical instants, including the exceptional week; document any legitimate source replacement prospectively. Causal admission and all-source date accounting must be corrected separately.
